quests.title: Grave-Gold
quests.description:
I'm Maud. I comb this sand for a living, and the living's been thin since the barrows opened.

The dead out here were buried with their gold, and now they walk about with it in their pockets. Coins with a king on them that nobody remembers. I've a buyer in the highlands who'll pay for every one, and I'm too old to argue with a wight over it.

They come up out of the west barrow and the east one. Bring me eight coins and I'll make it worth the trip.
quests.accept_text: The west barrow and the east one. Mind your feet on the way over, the shallows shift.
quests.turn_in_text:
Eight. Look at that king. Nobody's spent one of these in a thousand years, and now I'm going to.

You've earned your cut.

quests.title: Lights on the Barrows
quests.description:
You've seen the lights out on the barrows at night. Corpse-lights, my mother called them. They're not lights. They're the dead that couldn't find their bodies, and they lead the living ones out into the water.

I lost a boat to them last winter. I'd like to stop losing things.

Put out six of the lights, and six of the wights they keep lit for.
quests.accept_text: The barrows, west and east. Don't follow a light anywhere it wants you to go.
quests.turn_in_text: It's darker out there tonight. Good dark. The kind you can sleep in.

quests.title: The Brine King (Elite)
quests.description:
There's a fourth barrow, out on its own to the north. The King's. The others are his thanes, and they don't rest because he doesn't.

He walks the top of his barrow at low tide with his crown on, and he doesn't like visitors. I won't lie to you: I wouldn't go alone. I wouldn't go at all. But if anyone's going to put him back in the ground, it'll be somebody who brought friends.

His thanes stand round him. Cut through five and you'll find him.
quests.accept_text: North, out past the middle bar. Bring friends. I mean it.
quests.turn_in_text:
You did it. The water's gone still out there, first time since I came.

That's the best thing I own. Take it.

quests.title: Glass Teeth
quests.description:
The basilisks here grow glass on their backs. They lie in the hot sand and it fuses to them, a little more every year, till they're walking about wearing a fortune.

I make blades from it. Best edge you'll ever see, and it never rusts. But I've got one good leg left and I'm keeping it.

The shard fields, west of the mouth. Eight shards.
quests.accept_text: West of the mouth, where the sand shines. They'll see you coming. Let them.
quests.turn_in_text:
Feel the edge on that one. Careful. See?

I'll have one of these sharpened for you by the time you're back.

quests.title: Walking Kilns
quests.description:
Whatever burned this canyon didn't stop. It's still up on the rise to the north, walking about on its own, and every time one of them comes down the sand goes to glass under it and my camp gets smaller.

Kiln-walkers, I call them. Put out eight and I'll get a season's peace.
quests.accept_text: Up the rise to the north. Water won't help. Hitting them will.
quests.turn_in_text:
I could hear them stop. You don't notice a noise till it stops.

Here, for your trouble.

quests.title: Old Blister (Elite)
quests.description:
There's one basilisk up in the hollow at the north end that's more glass than beast. Old Blister. She's the reason I've got one good leg.

She's been growing that hide since before I was born, and nothing I own cuts it. Don't go alone. Take people you trust and go up through the basilisks round her, and when she opens her mouth, don't be in front of it.
quests.accept_text: North, into the hollow. Bring people. She'll take your leg too.
quests.turn_in_text:
You've no idea. You've no idea what that means.

I made this from the first shard I ever took off her. It's yours.

quests.title: Teeth in the Green Water
quests.description:
I'm Koji'ra. My grandmother told me about these shoals, and everybody laughed at her, and I came anyway. Now I'm the one nobody would believe.

The snappers own the water and the stalkers own the trees, and between them I can't get off this beach. Thin them out for me. Six of each.
quests.accept_text: The snappers are in the water round the landing. The stalkers are in the tangles east and west. Watch the branches.
quests.turn_in_text: I walked to the big island this morning and nothing tried to eat me. First time.

quests.title: Sap That Glows
quests.description:
The trees out here bleed light. The guardians on the big island carry it in them, and my grandmother said it came up from the roots of one tree, older than the isles.

I want to know if she was right. Bring me six of it and I'll read what's in it.
quests.accept_text: The big island. The guardians are slow, but they don't forget you.
quests.turn_in_text:
Look at it move. It's not sap at all. It's coming up from something, a long way down.

She was right. I knew she was right.

quests.title: Grandfather Mangrove (Elite)
quests.description:
There's one guardian on the big island bigger than the rest. Grandfather Mangrove, my grandmother called him, and she said he walks round the old tree the way a dog walks round a door it's guarding.

I'd like to see that door. I'm not getting past him, and you won't either, not alone. Bring friends. Cut through his guardians and put him down.
quests.accept_text: The big island, where the trees get older. Bring friends. He's been growing a long time.
quests.turn_in_text:
He's down. Now let's see what he was standing in front of.

Take this, you've earned it twice over.

quests.title: Nothing Bites Like a Lagoon
quests.description:
Fizzle Brassgut, treasure hunter, at your service. I've got a boat, a map and a lagoon full of drowned gods made of solid jade, and I can't get off this beach because every single thing in the water wants to eat me.

Crocs and serpents. Six of each and I'll cut you in.
quests.accept_text: They're all round the landing. You'll hear the crocs before you see them.
quests.turn_in_text: Look at that! I can see the water! I can see the TREASURE in the water!

quests.title: Small Pieces of God
quests.description:
The trolls that drowned with the idols carry bits of them. Shards. Chipped off for luck, I reckon, and it didn't work, did it?

The drowned ones on the west and east isles have them. Eight shards and I've got enough to buy a bigger boat.
quests.accept_text: The western and eastern isles. The hexers will try to put a curse on you. Don't let them.
quests.turn_in_text: Eight! These are going to make me so rich. Us. Us rich. Here, your share up front.

quests.title: The Idol-Keeper (Elite)
quests.description:
Bad news. The biggest idol, on the last isle up north, has a keeper. Zun'jal. Drowned with the rest of them and didn't let it slow him down one bit. He's got his hexers round him and he's not sharing.

I'm not asking you to go alone. I'm asking you to bring every friend you've got.
quests.accept_text: The last isle, north past the jade isles. Bring friends. Lots of friends.
quests.turn_in_text:
He's gone? He's GONE! Fizzle Brassgut, richest goblin in the jungle!

Take your pick, partner. You earned it.

quests.title: Things in the Sand
quests.description:
Rizzo Dustwhistle. My family's been looking for this caravan for four generations and I'm the one who found it. Of course I am.

Problem is it's full of scorpids and the people who were on it, who aren't people any more. Clear me a way in. Six of each.
quests.accept_text: The dunes by the landing, and the wagon graves west. Watch the sand, it moves.
quests.turn_in_text: I can see a wagon wheel sticking up out of the sand. Grandma's wagon wheel, maybe!

quests.title: The Manifest
quests.description:
The caravan's ledger got torn up when they went under. Every guard on that caravan was carrying a piece of it, because the Master didn't trust anybody.

The revenants in the market still have them. Eight pages and I'll know what's buried here, and where.
quests.accept_text: The drowned market, north of the dunes. The revenants carry them. They won't give them up.
quests.turn_in_text: Silk, spice, a dragon's egg... a DRAGON'S EGG? Oh, Grandma.

quests.title: The Last Caravan Master (Elite)
quests.description:
The ledger says the Master kept the good stuff in his own wagon, at the very back. And he's still in it. He still thinks he's delivering it.

The colossi at the gate keep people away from him, and he'll be harder than all of them. Bring a crew. Then I'll finally know what four generations of my family died looking for.
quests.accept_text: North, through the buried gate to the back of the caravan. Bring a crew.
quests.turn_in_text:
It's real. All of it. Four generations, and it's real.

Pick something. Pick two, I won't tell.

quests.title: What Fell In
quests.description:
I'm Brannoc. The ground opened under the Barrens and I came down on a rope to see why. The rope's gone now, and so is the way I came.

The hyenas came down the same way, and the quillboar were already here. Clear the floor for me. Six of each.
quests.accept_text: The sinkhole floor, and the thornwalls west of it.
quests.turn_in_text: The floor's quiet. I can hear the drums further in now. That isn't better.

quests.title: Prayer-Bones
quests.description:
The thornspeakers carry bones carved with prayers. I want to know who they're praying to down here, because something's answering.

Eight bones. The thornspeakers keep to the walls and the shrine-pool north.
quests.accept_text: The thornwalls west, and the shrine-pool north. They'll pray at you. Ignore it.
quests.turn_in_text: These are all one name, over and over. The Thorn-Mother. She's not alive. She doesn't need to be.

quests.title: The Thorn-Mother's Echo (Elite)
quests.description:
Her seat is at the north end, above everything. Her dead walk round it. And she walks among them, what's left of her.

She's why the ground opened. I'm sure of it. Put her down and maybe it closes again. Don't go alone.
quests.accept_text: North, to her seat. Bring friends. She'll sing and the thorns will listen.
quests.turn_in_text: The drums stopped. Thank you. I think I can find a way up now.

quests.title: Lights That Lie
quests.description:
I'm Ithrael. My grandmother put the seal on this glade and never spoke of it. I'm here to read what she wouldn't say.

The wisps lead people off the path and leave them. Put out eight of them before they put me out.
quests.accept_text: Along the shadowed path, near where you came in.
quests.turn_in_text: Darker. Honest dark, though. I'll take it.

quests.title: The Sentinels Who Stayed
quests.description:
The sentinels my grandmother left here are still on watch. They died on watch. They don't know they can stop.

And the satyrs came because the sentinels can't see them any more. Free six of the sentinels, and end six of the satyrs.
quests.accept_text: The silent grove west for the sentinels, the twisted hollow east for the satyrs.
quests.turn_in_text: They went quietly. I think they were glad. The satyrs weren't.

quests.title: The Unlit Priestess (Elite)
quests.description:
I've read it now. A priestess here prayed to Elune for something she shouldn't have, and Elune turned away, and the moon has not shone on this glade since.

She's still in the shrine at the north end, still praying. Go with friends and give her an answer.
quests.accept_text: North, to the sealed shrine. Bring friends. She won't stop praying long enough to talk.
quests.turn_in_text:
The clouds are thinning. Is that... look. Look up.

Thank you. Take whatever you like.

quests.title: Rams and Wings
quests.description:
Halvard Grey. I chase storms. This one never moves, which makes it either the easiest storm in the world to study or the most dangerous.

The rams charge anything that moves, and the harpies nest in the east ring. Six of each, so I can set up my rods.
quests.accept_text: The rams are on the crag path. The harpies nest east, in the ring.
quests.turn_in_text: My rods are up. Now we wait for the lightning. We won't wait long.

quests.title: Bottled Lightning
quests.description:
The stormlings carry shards with lightning still inside. If I can read eight of them I can tell you what's calling the storm.

They're thickest up on the thunder table.
quests.accept_text: North, on the thunder table. They'll shock you. That's how you know it's working.
quests.turn_in_text: It's the stone. The big one, at the very top. The storm isn't sitting here. It's being called.

quests.title: The Calling Stone (Elite)
quests.description:
The stone at the top calls the storm, and the wardens in the rings keep anyone from getting to it. Somebody made them for that. Somebody wanted this storm.

Break the stone. Bring people who don't mind being struck by lightning.
quests.accept_text: North, to the very top of the crag. Bring friends. Don't wear anything metal. Joking. Mostly.
quests.turn_in_text:
Look at that. Blue sky. First time in a hundred years, the old books say.

You earned this.

quests.title: The Grey Rows
quests.description:
I'm Marta. My family grew apples here before the plague. I died in that house over there, and when I woke up I walked straight back. Funny, that.

The scarecrows don't know me any more and the ghouls never did. Six of each, if you would.
quests.accept_text: The grey rows west of the gate. The scarecrows only look like they're not moving.
quests.turn_in_text: Thank you. I walked the rows just now. My father planted those.

quests.title: The Cider House
quests.description:
The pickers in the cider house are still pressing apples. Plagued apples. Somebody is going to drink that one day.

Stop the pickers, and the bats that eat the fallen fruit and carry it off. Six of each.
quests.accept_text: The cider house, east. The bats are everywhere. Look up.
quests.turn_in_text: No more cider. I never thought I'd be glad to say that.

quests.title: Old Bramley (Elite)
quests.description:
My father made the first scarecrow and named it Bramley after the apple. It stands under the old tree now with a scythe, and the plague's in it, and it doesn't stop.

Please put it down. Take friends. It was built to keep things away, and it's good at it.
quests.accept_text: North, under the old tree. Bring friends. It's bigger than it was.
quests.turn_in_text:
He's down. Father would have hated what it became. Thank you.

Take something. I've no use for any of it now.

quests.title: What the Roots Remember
quests.description:
I'm Ash'ka. Koji'ra's grandmother. I told her about this tree when she was small, and then I came to find it myself, and it kept me. I don't mind. It's beautiful down here.

The Darkspear who followed me down stopped listening to the roots and started speaking for them. They're wrong about what the tree wants. Quiet five of them, and the spiders that nest in the galleries.
quests.accept_text: Through the amber hollows and out along the roots. The spiders like the dark places between.
quests.turn_in_text: Listen. Hear that? That's the tree, not them. It's been a long time.

quests.title: The Sap-Mother (Elite)
quests.description:
In the heartwood there's a pool of sap that woke up. Amberheart. She was meant to feed the tree and she's started keeping it all for herself, and the tree is getting hungry.

She'll seal you in amber if she can. Bring friends who can cut you out.
quests.accept_text: The heartwood, in the middle of everything. You'll know it by the light.
quests.turn_in_text: The sap's running again. Can you feel it? Warm, all the way down.

quests.title: The Root-Father (Elite)
quests.description:
At the very bottom of the tree, which is the top of everything down here, the oldest root of all has woken up. The Root-Father. He was here before the isles were. He's angry that anyone found him.

And old Gnarl, out in the knotted dark, has been feeding him. Put them both back to sleep. Not alone. Never alone, not down here.
quests.accept_text: Up through the knotted deep to the root-father's bed. Gnarl lurks off to the west.
quests.turn_in_text:
He's sleeping. The whole tree just sighed. Did you hear it?

Take this. Then go and tell my granddaughter I'm happy here. She'll want to know.

quests.title: Nothing Left to Read
quests.description:
I was the librarian here. Before the Bloom. Before the Scourge. Before most things. I stayed because someone has to know where everything is.

The wraiths are what's left of the books the Bloom wrote over. The erasures are what's left of the readers. Give them rest. Six of each.
quests.accept_text: The outer stacks. Go round. Everything down here goes round.
quests.turn_in_text: Quieter. You can almost hear the pages turning. That's a good sound, down here.

quests.title: The Pages Underneath
quests.description:
The scholars drowned in the ink carry pages scraped clean. But a scraped page remembers. Bring me eight and I'll read what was on them first.

They walk the inner shelves. You'll have to find the way in. The gates are never where you'd want them.
quests.accept_text: The inner shelves. The gate into each ring is on a different side. Walk round.
quests.turn_in_text: Here. Under the Bloom's writing, under the one before that. A name. The Keeper's. He's still here, at the top, still trying to finish the first page.

quests.title: The First Page (Elite)
quests.description:
The Keeper has been trying to finish the first page for longer than there have been people to read it. The Editor at the heart of the vault strikes out every word he writes. They will never finish. And while they try, nothing down here can rest.

End it. Both of them. Take everyone you trust.

objectives.target: The Keeper of the First Page

quests.accept_text: The Editor sits at the heart of the rings. The Keeper reads alone, beyond the top of the vault.
quests.turn_in_text:
It's finished. Not the page. The trying.

Take one of these. I've been keeping them for whoever finally did it.

quests.title: The Hanging Wood
quests.description:
I'm Ilsabet. I came here to study the mere and I've stayed because I can't leave it unfinished.

The spiders in the west wood hang their kills in the pines, and then the kills come down again on their own. I'd like fewer of both.

Eight spiders. The wood west of the track.
quests.accept_text: West of the track, where the pines are thickest. Look up before you look down.
quests.turn_in_text: Quieter. I can hear the water again, which isn't better, but at least I know where it is.

quests.title: Mere-Water
quests.description:
The wraiths at the mere are made of it. The water, I mean. If you break one apart there's a little left that won't drain away, and that's what I need. It remembers things, and I want to know what.

Six vials. The wraiths keep to the mere and the shrine above it.
quests.accept_text: The mere, and the shrine north of it. Don't drink any. I know you weren't going to.
quests.turn_in_text:
Six. Hold one up to the light. See the shapes? Those are the pines, from before.

Thank you. Truly.

quests.title: What Weeps
quests.description:
The worgen here don't hunt. They walk the track and weep, and if you get between one and the water it'll tear you apart to get past. The trees in the drowned copse have started doing the same.

I've read enough to know they're not the cause. But they're in the way of the cause. Eight worgen and four of the rotbarks.
quests.accept_text: The track, and the copse east of the mere. They won't stop crying. Don't let it get to you.
quests.turn_in_text: It's not the worgen. It never was. It's her.

quests.title: The Widow of the Mere (Elite)
quests.description:
She drowned herself in the mere after the pines died, and she took the wood with her. That's what the vials showed me. Everything here weeps because she does.

She rises out of the water when the fog's thickest, with her wraiths round her. I can't fight her. You can't either, not alone. Bring people who aren't afraid of crying things.
quests.accept_text: The mere. Wait for the fog. Bring friends, and don't listen when she says your name.
quests.turn_in_text:
The fog's thinning. I can see the far shore.

I think I can go home now. Take this. I won't need it where I'm going.
